reader.requirement: At --std 85 OPEN EXTEND of an indexed file must be refused unless the file's access mode is sequential (explicit or default); EXTEND on a sequential-access indexed file is legal and appends.
reader.edition-search: read BindOpen (comments name it edition-agnostic) and CheckOpenModeForFile: the only DialectLevel read there picks the FORMAT clause citation in the I-O arm, not reached by EXTEND; no ConstructRegistry/VersionConformancePass gate on OPEN EXTEND
reader.witnesses-cover: part: pb318-open-extend-access-linage covers a non-sequential access refusal; the accepted sequential form and its run-time behaviour are not exercised

probes.printed: error COBOL2372: OPEN EXTEND 'IXF' — the file's access mode is DYNAMIC; EXTEND requires sequential access
error COBOL2372: ... access mode is RANDOM ...
OPEN-MISSING FS=35 / OPEN-EXT FS=00 / SEQERR FS=21 / AAAADATA01 / CCCCDATA03 / EOF
probes.expected: accepted; EXTEND of an unavailable file is unsuccessful (table on IX-24), EXTEND appends, a key out of ascending order is a sequence error

reader.notes: There is one edition-agnostic screen on the file's access mode. The 2023 rule adds a LINAGE conjunct that does not matter for an indexed file, because LINAGE is not in the indexed FD format. The run-time append and failed-open behaviour are correct.

refuter.evidence: --std 85. r3_mixed_dyn.cob: OPEN INPUT SQF EXTEND IXF (IXF dynamic) gives COBOL2372 on IXF. r3_list_rnd.cob: OPEN EXTEND SQF IXF (IXF random, the second of a file list) gives COBOL2372, so each file of the list is screened. r3_default_opt.cob: SELECT OPTIONAL with no ACCESS clause compiles and runs, 'OPEN-EXT FS=05 / AAAA FS=00', so the default sequential access is admitted and an absent optional file is created by EXTEND. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:IX.4.4.3 SR1  (4.4.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR1'.
